finding.title: failed runtime decrypt can leave partial plaintext at the final restore path and can overwrite a previously good restored archive
finding.root_cause: both restore scripts pass the final destination directly to gpg --output; there is no temporary sibling + success-only atomic promotion and no failed-output cleanup
finding.scope_note: The reproduction proves shell failure semantics on Linux and the source-level direct-final-output pattern in both scripts. It does not claim native Windows filesystem atomicity; the PowerShell fix still needs a native Windows gate when ZERO-MINUTE permits one.

candidate_fix.strategy: decrypt to a random temporary sibling in runtime-state-restored, delete temp on failure, then rename/move to final destination only after gpg exit 0; preserve previous good final file on failure

next_gate: materialize exact scripts + regression harness in normal git workspace; Linux shell dynamic test; PowerShell static contract; later one native Windows restore atomicity gate without starting a new digest fanout
